chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the kohl (eye powder) for the one in Ihram. He said: As for the blackness (kohl), then no. But (yes) with the Sabr and Al-Hudhud.

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in Ihram (ritual state)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using kohl while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of kohl for the Muhrim is specific to its use as cosmetic adornment (typically black), while medicinal or natural powders like Sabr and Al-Hudhud remain permissible. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that the restriction in Ihram targets vanity and beautification rather than general utility or healing, reflecting the practical flexibility within ritual purity laws.
